description: THE SUBSCRIPT NO COBOL TABLE COULD ADDRESS, AND THE OUTERMOST OF THIS DIRECTORY'S FOUR SUBSCRIPT-BOUNDARY CASES. Read the series in order to see what each one isolates: case06 drives a subscript below the valued span, case08 one inside the declared table but past the count, and this case one far beyond the declared table altogether - 99, the largest value WS-OPTION PIC 9(02) at app/cbl/COMEN01C.cbl:46 can hold. Together they pin gate G33 from both ends, which matters because COBOL subscripts are 1-based and Java indices are 0-based, and an off-by-one in that conversion is invisible in the middle of a table and only shows at its edges. The three-term guard at :127-129 is reached and its terms are evaluated in source order, which is gate G30: '99' IS numeric, so term one, WS-OPTION IS NOT NUMERIC, is false; term two, WS-OPTION > CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT, is TRUE, because the count is the 10 that app/cpy/COMEN02Y.cpy:21 declares as PIC 9(02) VALUE 10 and the test is a strict greater-than; term three, WS-OPTION = ZEROS, is never reached. It is therefore the same term case08 fires and a different term from case07, which fires the first on the non-numeric '1x' - the point of pinning three separate cases on one three-term guard is that an implementation reordering the terms, or collapsing them into a single range check, passes some and fails others rather than passing all. Line 130 moves 'Y' into WS-ERR-FLG, which is the 88 ERR-FLG-ON condition at :41, lines 131-132 move the thirty-seven-character invalid-option literal into WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) at :38, and line 133 performs SEND-MENU-SCREEN, so the first and only screen image is painted here. Nothing is normalised on the way in, and that is a deliberate contrast with case06: the descending test-before scan at :117-121 examines OPTIONI OF COMEN1AI(2:1), finds the '9' already non-blank and exits immediately with WS-IDX = 2, so the two-byte move at :122 into the PIC X(02) JUST RIGHT receiver at :45 needs no right-justification and the INSPECT REPLACING ALL ' ' BY '0' at :123 is a no-op - where case06's leading blank is precisely what that INSPECT turns into a zero. Line 125 echoes the rejected value unchanged, so OPTIONO is '99' and not spaces, not '00' and not the clamped '12' an implementation that silently bounded the input would produce. Then the substance of the case. PERFORM SEND-MENU-SCREEN returns, so control falls through to the filter at :136-137, which is NOT guarded by IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON and so evaluates CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE(99) with the error flag already set. The commarea supplies CDEMO-USER-TYPE 'U', which makes the first conjunct CDEMO-USRTYP-USER true and forces the second to actually be read - with 'A' the conjunction would short-circuit and the subscript would never be touched, so the user type is load-bearing here rather than incidental. CDEMO-MENU-OPT is declared OCCURS 12 TIMES at app/cpy/COMEN02Y.cpy:88, so 99 addresses nothing at all: not merely an unvalued slot but an offset outside the group item. A reviewer can check the geometry by eye. Each entry is CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NUM PIC 9(02) plus CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME PIC X(35) plus CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME PIC X(08) plus CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE PIC X(01) at :89-92, so 2 + 35 + 8 + 1 = 46 bytes; the data division gives VALUE clauses to ten entries at :25-84, 10 x 46 = 460 bytes, while CDEMO-MENU-OPTIONS REDEFINES CDEMO-MENU-OPTIONS-DATA at :87 spans twelve, 12 x 46 = 552 bytes - so 92 bytes, exactly slots 11 and 12, have no backing data, and slot 99 would begin 4,508 bytes into a 552-byte redefinition of a 460-byte item. Compiled without SSRANGE, COBOL computes that offset and reads whatever bytes happen to be there; it does not fail. Java would throw IndexOutOfBoundsException, and a crash the source does not produce is itself a parity violation, so the read must be bounded and must yield nothing. That oversized REDEFINES and that ungated filter are legacy defects and both are preserved rather than repaired: the access is bounded, the logic is not corrected, and the unreachable 'A' arm stays unreachable. Line 145's IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON is then false, so the whole navigation block at :146-164 is skipped, and every one of its side effects is absent from the expectation for that reason: no EXEC CICS XCTL, so no successor is named and the termination is the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID of :107-110 rather than a transfer; CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT stays 1 because the MOVE ZEROS of :151 never runs; CDEMO-FROM-TRANID and CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM keep their inbound values because :147-148 never run; and ERRMSGC is never overridden, because the MOVE DFHGREEN of :158 sits inside that same block. What the case asserts most sharply is the pair expectedReturnCode 0 and exactly one entry in expectedMessages, and both are load-bearing. COMEN01C contains no RETURN-CODE, no CALL 'CEE3ABD' and no ABEND anywhere in its 282 lines, so a faithful run completes normally even though the filter read far outside the table: an implementation that let an IndexOutOfBoundsException escape - a bare get(option - 1), or an array sized to the active count of ten - cannot produce return code 0. The count of one is meaningful rather than incidental, because :127-134, :136-143 and :157-164 are three sequential IF statements rather than exclusive branches, so two images really are structurally possible on this path, as case10 demonstrates; here the second must not appear, and the message left standing on the screen must be the option rejection rather than the No access text an implementation reading stray bytes as 'A' would have produced. In honesty about what this case does not prove: it does not prove that the filter is ungated. An implementation that wrongly gated it on the error flag would pass this case too, because the shipped table's ten CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE columns are every one of them 'U' (:29, :35, :41, :47, :53, :59, :65, :72, :78, :84) and the filter's true arm is unreachable from real data - ungatedness is case10's to prove, on a stub table, and the filter's true arm belongs to case11 and case12. What this case decisively proves is boundedness at a subscript outside the declared OCCURS range, and the survival of the invalid-option message past a filter that ran anyway. The ten forty-character option lines are still built, because SEND-MENU-SCREEN at :182 performs BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS at :185 before the SEND, and that loop at :238-239 runs only while WS-IDX is not greater than the count of ten - so OPTN011O and OPTN012O, whose EVALUATE arms do exist at :269-272, are never written and stay as the MOVE LOW-VALUES of :89 left them, forty X'00' characters each rather than forty spaces. The loop's WHEN OTHER CONTINUE at :273-274 is the arm a subscript like this one would meet if the loop could ever reach it, and it never can, because its bound is the count rather than the OCCURS. No highlight is expected and none may be: COMEN01C does not copy CSSETATY - its COPY list at :50-61 is COCOM01Y, COMEN02Y, COMEN01, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CSUSR01Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA - and the DFHRED-plus-asterisk error highlight that copybook applies belongs to COACTUPC, its only consumer. DFHRED appears nowhere in this program's source; the DFHRED recorded against ERRMSGC here is the mnemonic of the COLOR=RED the map itself declares at app/bms/COMEN01.bms:154-157, reported unchanged precisely because the program never touched the attribute - which is why the error is signalled by the message text and the error flag alone. Gate G38's pair is therefore honoured through the ENTER and REENTER split rather than through any colour: this is a REENTER-side case, arriving with CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT 1 so that :87 sends it down the RECEIVE-and-validate path, and the message and the flag become non-default only there. No thank-you line is expected either; COTTL01Y's CCDA-THANK-YOU and CSMSG01Y's CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU are both copied in and neither is ever referenced. inputs, expectedWrites and expectedFinalState are all empty, and that is a positive assertion rather than an omission: COMEN01C performs no dataset access at all - it declares WS-USRSEC-FILE at :39 and copies CSUSR01Y at :58, but there is no SELECT, no FD and no file operand among its five EXEC CICS commands - and case18 pins that absence for the whole directory. User type is inbound only and is never re-verified, because :150's MOVE SEC-USR-TYPE TO CDEMO-USER-TYPE is commented out, so this single PIC X(01) comparison is the entire authorisation mechanism, exactly as the legacy program leaves it; no lookup, no re-derivation and no hashing is introduced here, and none may be. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:33, the instant COMEN01C's own version footer at :281 carries, and US-ASCII is named explicitly rather than left to a platform default; POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :212-231 does run on this path, since SEND-MENU-SCREEN performs it at :184, so CURDATE and CURTIME are genuinely produced in the MM/DD/YY and HH:MM:SS shapes of app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy:30-41, and all twenty cases in this directory pin that same instant so no two can differ by their clock. The clock is carried on screenRequest.pinnedClock rather than among the job parameters, because ParityCase refuses jobParameters on anything other than a BATCH_JOB and this case is a SERVICE - admin.MainMenuService constructed and called as a plain object, with no MockMvc, no servlet container and no JobLauncher between the assertion and the code, which is gate G51. One divergence from this file's own assignment brief is recorded here rather than absorbed silently. The brief described option 11 for this case and an allocation of 12 and 13 to case10 and case11. The frozen sibling contract had already settled that ground differently and this file defers to it: case08.json drives option 11 and its description names case09 as the one far beyond the table; COMEN01CParityTest.java:1073 routes case09 to runOutOfRangeSubscript, which asserts the subscript is greater than OCCURS_TABLE_SIZE - twelve - so option 11 would fail the very runner that executes this fixture; and case10 and case11 drive options 03 and 01 to reach the ungated filter and its true arm rather than any subscript boundary. Option 99 fires the same second validation term the brief asks for, keeps this case distinct from case08 instead of duplicating it, and pins the outer end of the boundary series the brief was reaching for. No user-specified rules govern this work - review_rules returns exactly No user rules provided - so nothing here is authorised by a rule; the enterprise practices of the plan are held to instead, and this note exists because one of them requires a conflict to be documented rather than quietly resolved. Every expected value here is statically derived - read out of the COBOL paragraph that produces it and cross-checked against the option table and 46-byte entry layout of app/cpy/COMEN02Y.cpy, the sixteen-field 160-byte commarea of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, the xxxI and xxxO PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COMEN01.CPY, the DFHMDF definitions of app/bms/COMEN01.bms and the CM00-to-COMEN01C binding of app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:399-400 - and none of it was captured from an execution of the legacy program, which is empirically impossible here: no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, no Language Environment CEE services, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR absent from the repository altogether. That substitution of provenance is escalated rather than absorbed (risk R-A).
